description: This repo maintains its OWN toolchain, narrowly. It used to carry `enabled: false` (2026-06-03), which kept Renovate off it entirely — and the cost was measurable: its workflow actions drifted for months with nobody to notice.

The scope is deliberately narrow via `enabledManagers`: only `github-actions` and `npm`, which sees nothing but package.json (the CI validator). `default.json` is the preset that the consumer repos extend UNPINNED from this branch, so main is production for them — it must never be moved by a bot. That holds twice over: no Renovate manager matches `default.json` at all, and `enabledManagers` excludes the `renovate-config` manager that would otherwise match this very file.

Automerge is off by default and on only where a bump cannot reach a consumer (2026-11-20). The catch-all packageRule below sets `automerge: false` for everything, cancelling the shared preset's automerge for patch/pin/digest; the two rules after it win (the last matching rule wins) and turn it back on for minor/patch bumps of the CI validator (`renovate` in package.json) and for minor/patch/digest/pin bumps of the workflow actions. Those PRs only change package.json, package-lock.json and `.github/workflows`, never what consumers extend: no enabled manager matches `default.json` or `config-repo.json` (see above). They still wait out the preset's 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` and merge only once CI is green; majors keep human review. `platformAutomerge` is NOT a guardrail: it only decides who performs the merge, not whether one happens.

The validator that gates the preset is a devDependency in package.json, installed by CI with `npm ci` from package-lock.json, so its whole tree is pinned by integrity hash. Renovate bumps it through the `npm` manager like any dependency. Until 2026-09-22 it was `npm install -g renovate@<version>` kept current by a regex manager, which pinned renovate but let its transitive tree float on every run. Lock-file maintenance is OFF here: the preset turns it on with automerge, and this branch is production for every consumer; the lockfile moves only with a renovate bump.

`postUpdateOptions: ["npmDedupe"]` (2026-11-13): the bump to renovate 44.221.5 came out of the bot with a lockfile that `npm ci` rejects. The bot's `npm install --package-lock-only` kept the old hoisted `@opentelemetry/api` 1.9.1 at the root and nested the 1.10.0 that renovate now pins under `renovate/node_modules`, so the OpenTelemetry 3.x packages, whose peer range is `>=1.10.0 <1.11.0`, resolved to 1.9.1. A clean regeneration with npm 8 to 11 hoists 1.10.0 and passes; the bot's exact run could not be reproduced. `npmDedupe` makes the bot pass `--prefer-dedupe`, which favours one shared copy over keeping a stale hoisted one. It applies to this repo only: consumers extend `default.json`, never this file.

packageRules.description: Default for this repo: no automerge, overriding the shared preset's automerge for patch/pin/digest. Only the two narrower rules below turn it back on.
Minor/patch bumps of the CI validator automerge once CI is green: they change package.json and package-lock.json only, never a preset.
Non-major bumps of the workflow actions automerge once CI is green: they change `.github/workflows` only, never a preset.
